subtype: Approach: hiding a mistake out of embarrassment [Pitfall]
passage: On Monday evening in London, Amara clicked a link in a message that said the school account had a problem. The page looked right, and Amara typed the password before thinking. Then the stomach dropped. A face went hot. Surely nobody would ever need to know. For two days Amara said nothing, and lay awake, hoping that it would just go away. On Wednesday Selin, in the same class, showed Amara a message that had come from Amara's account: a strange note asking for money. “Was this you?” Selin asked. Amara's throat closed. Then it all came out. They went together to Amara's mother, and the password was changed that night, but the account had been used for two days.

qa.q: How many days did Amara stay silent?
What was Amara feeling that kept the silence going for two days?
qa.a: Shame: Amara felt the face go hot and hoped nobody would ever need to know.

qa.q: What should Amara have done straight away, and why?
qa.a: Tell a trusted adult and change the password at once, since speed limits what a scammer can do with the account.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Selin?
qa.a: Selin received a strange money request from Amara's account and was suspicious and worried, and by asking directly helped bring the problem into the open.

grounding: After clicking a fake link and entering a password, a teen says nothing for two days out of shame, giving scammers time.

subtype: Approach: hiding a mistake out of embarrassment [Pitfall]
passage:
On Monday, in the school computer lab, Sumit clicked a link in his school email that said “Password expiring, verify now” and typed his password into the page. The page went blank. His stomach dropped. He closed the tab and said nothing.
He said nothing on Tuesday either. Every time he thought of telling Yamini Ma'am, the lab in-charge, he pictured the whole class hearing that he'd fallen for it.
On Wednesday morning, three classmates came to Yamini Ma'am confused. Emails from Sumit's account were asking them to share their own passwords “for a group project”. Two had already done it.
Yamini Ma'am called him over. He admitted everything, red-faced. She reset his account and the other two on the spot, and said, “On Monday it would have been one account. Now it's three. Next time, come to me in the first minute. Nobody gets scolded for that.”

qa.q: What did the fake email say?
Why did Sumit stay silent on Tuesday?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and afraid of the whole class hearing he had fallen for it, so embarrassment outweighed the risk.

qa.q: What should Sumit have done on Monday, and why?
qa.a: Tell Yamini Ma'am in the first minute, so the password could be reset before anyone else was targeted.

qa.q: How are the classmates affected by the delay?
qa.a: They get emails from what looks like a classmate's account, and two lose control of their own accounts, so the damage spreads.

grounding: Shows a teen hiding a password slip for two days out of shame, which lets scammers use the account before it is secured.

subtype: Approach: hiding a mistake out of embarrassment [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Gopika Didi,
I owe you the real story, not just the sorry I said on the phone.
On Friday I got a message that looked like it came from the photo app, saying my account would be locked. I typed my password into the page it opened. The moment I pressed enter, I knew: the page had a strange web address. I felt so embarrassed that I told no one. I kept thinking I'd fix it myself somehow, and then I didn't.
On Sunday someone using my account messaged you pretending to be me, asking for a code “to recover my account”. You trusted me, so you sent it, and they got into yours.
If I had told Papa on Friday, he would have helped me change the password that night, and you'd never have got that message. Two days of hiding did this, not the click.
I've told Papa now. We changed everything and reported the account together.
Nitin

qa.q: When did someone message Gopika Didi from Nitin's account?
How does Nitin feel writing this letter?
qa.a: Nitin feels guilty and full of regret, seeing that two days of hiding, not the click, let the harm reach Gopika Didi.

qa.q: What should Nitin do if something like this happens again?
qa.a: Tell Papa or another trusted adult at once, so the password is changed that same night, before anyone else is targeted.

qa.q: How might Gopika Didi feel reading the real story?
qa.a: She may still be upset about her account, but the honest letter may help her feel respected rather than betrayed.

grounding: Shows a teen hiding a password slip for two days out of embarrassment, giving scammers time to use the account and reach a relative.
